items.label: Synthetic AD-like section, higher burden (schematic)
items.studentNote: A made-up practice section with many lesions, not real tissue; it plays the positive control, but no one has checked how it stains.
items.notes: Synthetic stand-in for a characterized positive staining control. Nothing about it has been characterized; a real control requires a real section with known staining history. Schematic lesion distribution for teaching. Not derived from any real specimen.

items.label: Synthetic AD-like section, lower burden (schematic)
items.studentNote: A made-up practice section with fewer lesions, not real tissue; it shows that the same darkness can come from different amounts.
items.notes: Synthetic experimental section with lower schematic lesion presence than SPEC-SYN-AD-01. Under an extended development endpoint its plaque-core visibility matches SPEC-SYN-AD-01 at SOP defaults: the same darkness from different amounts. Schematic lesion distribution for teaching. Not derived from any real specimen.

items.label: Synthetic negative comparison section (schematic)
items.studentLabel: Negative comparison · no plaques or tangles
items.studentNote: A made-up practice section, not real tissue; it plays the negative comparison, but its axons still stain.
items.notes: Synthetic stand-in for a negative biological comparison: no plaques, tangles or neuropil threads, but normal structures (axons) still stain, so it is not expected to be blank. Nothing about it has been characterized. Not derived from any real specimen.

items.label: Synthetic high-amount, low-reduction-site section (schematic)
items.studentNote: Not real tissue: it has lots of target, but few reduction sites (spots that turn silver ions into metal) limit the signal.
items.notes: Synthetic experimental section with high schematic presence at every site but few reduction sites, so deposit is limited by site chemistry rather than by amount: more target, less signal. Schematic device for teaching intensity versus amount. Not derived from any real specimen.
